identity.title: PRISM: Gauge-Invariant Tangent-Space Differentially Private LoRA

problem.claim: Apply differential privacy to LoRA fine-tuning while controlling perturbations of the represented low-rank update.

gap.claim: Directly perturbing LoRA factors is problematic because their factorization is non-identifiable, making induced update noise gauge-dependent and potentially unboundedly amplified.

contributions.claim: PRISM is an intrinsic, gauge-invariant DP mechanism for LoRA that avoids bilinear noise amplification and supports efficient low-dimensional noise sampling.
The method provides a closed-form characterization of effective intrinsic noise on the update matrix and standard (ε,δ)-DP guarantees.
A DP-aware, gauge-invariant adaptive update rule is introduced to prevent adaptive optimization from amplifying injected privacy noise.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish PRISM as gauge-invariant by construction, with intrinsic noise handling and an adaptive update rule designed for gauge-invariant private LoRA.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that naive DP-LoRA can produce unbounded noise amplification on the represented update matrix.
The authors report standard (ε,δ)-DP guarantees for PRISM.
The authors report that the adaptive update rule improves numerical stability in practice.

narrative_sequence.summary: DP-SGD applied to LoRA is presented as a natural privacy-preserving fine-tuning approach.
LoRA’s non-identifiable factorization means direct factor perturbations depend on the gauge and can amplify noise without bound.
PRISM applies intrinsic, gauge-invariant perturbations and uses an efficient low-dimensional sampler.
A closed-form intrinsic-noise characterization enables stable privacy-utility trade-offs through bounded, gauge-invariant perturbations.
The paper states DP guarantees and adds a gauge-invariant adaptive rule intended to improve numerical stability.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a representation symmetry—non-identifiability—to gauge-dependent perturbations, then designs the privacy mechanism on the intrinsic update rather than directly on arbitrary factors.

lessons.interpretation: When parameterizations contain equivalent representations, analyzing and perturbing the represented object can make guarantees less dependent on coordinates.
lessons.application: For another reparameterized model, explicitly identify its symmetry, show how coordinate-level noise changes under that symmetry, and formulate the mechanism on the invariant object.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the invariant object is inaccessible, too costly to sample from, or does not support the required privacy accounting.

unknowns: The abstract gives no datasets, baselines, quantitative stability results, or experimental conditions.
The stated DP guarantees and bounded-noise characterization are not independently verifiable from the abstract alone.
The extent and conditions of the reported practical numerical-stability improvement are unspecified.

editorial_revisions.before: A closed-form intrinsic-noise description is used to frame bounded privacy–utility trade-offs.
editorial_revisions.after: A closed-form intrinsic-noise characterization enables stable privacy-utility trade-offs through bounded, gauge-invariant perturbations.
